attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter post.

semantics.note: 'Will undoubtedly help' is firm. The forecast is that AI helps large firms monetize and interrupt users more. The hedged clause about complete corporate control is correctly left out.

contract.note: Counting a large firm putting paid placements inside an AI-mediated experience as 'more monetized and more interrupted' is an ordinary reading of the words, and it doesn't stretch them. An aggregate-exposure reading would need different evidence; the contract flags this.

evidence.note: Dated Google rollout record (Oct 2024): after testing, ads inside AI Overviews went live for US mobile users. This is a new paid placement inside an AI answer. It is a company disclosure, but it describes an actual rollout.
Google's claim that users are more satisfied is about the wider experience. It doesn't contradict the added commercial placement.

reviews.rationale: Firm open-ended forecast. The early-resolution rule is met by Google's dated Oct 2024 rollout of paid ads inside AI Overviews, a large corporation adding commercial placements inside an AI-mediated activity. Google's satisfaction claim does not contradict this.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The testable part is the firm statement that the internet already is low-quality service journalism and/or ecommerce marketing. 'Porridge' is a metaphor, but the claim underneath is an observation.

contract.note: Reading it as 'widespread in ordinary internet use' is a fair, ordinary reading of a hyperbolic statement. The prevalence threshold and the observation window are the evaluator's choices, as the contract flags.

evidence.note: ANA study of made-for-advertising sites covers Sept 2022 to Jan 2023 and measures ad impressions, not content prevalence across the internet. Different period and metric, so context only.

reviews.rationale: The contract requires representative evidence of how common such content was across ordinary internet use in June 2023. The packet has only an ad-impression study from a different period and population. Neither support nor contradiction is established.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The firm claim is that the commercial content mill is already full of material made for Google traffic. The hedged 'AI might' is correctly kept as an unscored qualifier.

contract.note: Reading 'full of crap' as substantial, recurring low-value SEO content within the commercial publishing ecosystem is fair and ordinary, and it matches the surrounding paragraphs.

evidence.note: Independent Verge investigation (June 15, 2023) documents padded text written only for search engines, a producer explaining why, and outlets mass-producing SEO-bait articles. This meets the support condition.

reviews.rationale: Contemporary independent reporting with producer interviews documents scaled, deliberate production of low-value content aimed at Google traffic in the target window. The packet contains no counterevidence. No market share is required.
